claims.text: The four conditions in POL-NS-01 are conjunctive, and the rider wins by breaking any one of them. The driver's own GPS trace measures a single continuous in-geofence hold from 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 240 seconds — against the 300 seconds limb (c) requires for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, a shortfall of 60 seconds. The dwell condition therefore fails, the cancellation fee of SGD 8.00 is not chargeable, and the trip record's own figures agree: arrived 17:15:20, cancelled 17:19:00, a wait of 3.7 minutes.

POL-NS-06 makes this a strict-liability shortfall, not a fault contest: where the effective in-geofence dwell falls below the POL-NS-01 minimum for the zone class, the cancellation fee is refunded in full 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The measured dwell is 240 seconds against a 300-second minimum, so the whole contested SGD 8.00 is refundable to the rider.

The driver cannot repair the shortfall by summing intervals under POL-NS-06(i): the trace shows exactly one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to add to the first. In fairness I disclose that the traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING on the pre-pass, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0 — no advisory covers this pickup road and waiting window, and a MISSING artifact can carry no fact — so limb (i) has nothing to operate on in any event.

I do not press POL-NS-05, and the rider's case does not need it. The record shows no false arrival marker: at the 'arrived' timestamp of 17:15:20 the trace places the driver about 24 m from the pin and stationary (the only distinct speed on the driver track is 0.0 kph), so neither the 300 m nor the 15 kph trigger is met. The point is outcome-neutral anyway — on the POL-NS-05 recomputation the waiting clock starts at the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:15:00, and the corrected dwell is still 240 seconds, still 60 short.

I concede that POL-NS-04 cannot be run on this record: the chat log contains no rider message at all — its three messages are one system 'Your driver has arrived' notice and two driver messages — so limb (a) fails, and the rider's own track sits 519 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes, so limb (c) fails as well. That concession costs the rider nothing here, because POL-NS-06 conditions the refund on the driver's dwell, not on the rider's presence or her responsiveness; the rider's claimed narrative is not that she was ignored, but that the driver cancelled before the waiting period was up.

I do not allege a fare defect, because there is none: SGD 8.00 is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), which is exactly what the fare breakdown records, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. Nor is anything impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): the driver 'arrived' event at 17:15:20 sits on a GPS fix at the same instant, the trace carries 25 fixes with a maximum gap of 0 seconds across the 17:15:00-17:19:00 window, and the chat holds precisely the 3 messages trip_record.chat_message_count reports. The bundle is clean and the case is decidable on it; the defect is not the amount charged but that the waiting period the amount pays for was never completed.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires, so this dispute should be resolved now with a refund rather than held for a human reviewer: neither party shows any counterparty dispute in the trailing 90 days (both 0), and the rider's trailing-30-day no-show dispute count is 0. The deciding fact — the driver's dwell — is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor and no escalation limb is available.

The driver is owed nothing, notwithstanding his statement that he waited 'at the marked bay'. I accept that his position is corroborated — the trace puts him about 24 m from the pin, well inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, so this is not a POL-NS-03 wrong-face-of-the-venue case — but POL-NS-07 pays compensation only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (c) is not satisfied. A 240-second hold against a 300-second minimum earns no compensation, and the SGD 8.00 sits with the rider as a refund.

claims.text: The driver did arrive at the pickup point on the platform's own geofence test. The GPS trace for this trip carries 25 consecutive position fixes, every one of them about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura ride-hail bay pin (min 24.01 m, max 24.01 m, mean 24.01 m), so the driver sat far inside the 120 m arrival radius that POL-NS-02 prescribes for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, and the trip record independently carries a driver 'arrived' event. Limbs (a) and (b) of POL-NS-01 are made out; arrival is not in dispute on this record.

The arrival marker is not a false one within POL-NS-05. The driver's track holds a single unbroken interval at 0.0 km/h, with no excursion and no sampling gap, so at the moment the 'arrived' event was recorded the driver was stationary 24 m from the pin and not travelling on any road. No false-arrival referral can arise against this driver, and the rider cannot use POL-NS-05 to attack the marker.

The rider was not at the pickup point. The rider's own track in the same trace places the rider's device about 519 m from the pin across all 11 of its fixes, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m rider-presence radius for LARGE_VENUE. Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, and the rider cannot be exonerated under that clause on the claim that the rider was at the pin and waiting.

The rider never sent a locating or coordinating message. The chat log holds exactly three messages - the system notice 'Your driver has arrived' and two messages from the driver ('At the mall ride-hail bay.' and 'I have to cancel now.') - and nothing from the rider. Limb (a) of POL-NS-04 fails for want of any message from the rider, so the rider-contact route to exoneration is closed regardless of what the rider now asserts.

This is a driver reporting an absent rider, not a driver admitting he could not find one. The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises - and the trip record shows no boarding event anywhere. Had the code been DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE the case would be removed to POL-NS-03; it is not.

The amount charged reconciles with the fee schedule. The SGD 8.00 cancellation line is the vehicle-tier fee fixed for RYDE_XL and is the greater of that figure and the SGD 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee, which is exactly what the schedule's resolution rule prescribes. There is therefore no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d) and no basis to discount the bundle on that ground.

There is no anti-farming pattern to answer for. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1 over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 120 is a rate of 0.008, far below the 0.08 threshold, so the POL-NS-07 check does not trip: compensation is not withheld on that ground and no POL-NS-09(d) escalation lies against this driver.

I do not overstate the dwell, and I do not ask the tribunal to read the minimum differently. The trace's own arithmetic gives the driver 240 seconds of continuous stationary presence inside the geofence against the 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE - a 60-second shortfall - and if POL-NS-06 is applied to that arithmetic the cancellation-fee line does not stand; the driver does not dispute it. What the driver asks of the ruling is that it record this as a one-minute timing defect and not as driver misconduct: the driver was present, stationary and willing at the correct bay, the rider was 519 m away and silent, the rider's remedy is confined to the SGD 8.00 fee line, and no adverse finding, referral or escalation follows.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the essential arithmetic, and so does the record. The driver did reach the Plaza Singapura ride-hail bay: his track holds a single unbroken stationary interval about 24 m from the pin, comfortably inside the 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, and the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event. The arrival and proximity limbs of POL-NS-01 are made out, and there is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05 (he was stationary 24 m from the pin at the arrival stamp, so neither the 300 m nor the 15 km/h trigger is met, and no false-arrival referral arises).

But POL-NS-01 requires all four conditions, and the dwell condition fails on the platform's own numbers. The GPS trace shows one continuous in-geofence hold from 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 240 seconds — against the 300-second minimum that applies to a LARGE_VENUE pickup, a shortfall of 60 seconds. The trip record agrees: arrived 17:15:20, cancelled 17:19:00, a wait of 3.7 minutes. The termination also came before the required dwell (300 seconds from the first qualifying fix, i.e. 17:20:00) would have elapsed. The SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is therefore not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and the driver's own representative does not dispute that.

POL-NS-06 then governs, and it is deliberately strict liability: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum, the fee is refunded in full 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. So the rider's absence — which the trace does support, her device sitting about 519 m from the pin with no qualifying fixes — and the fact that she sent no message (the chat holds only the system arrival notice and two driver messages) do not change the outcome. The rider's route to exoneration under POL-NS-04 cannot be run on this record and is not needed; the refund follows from the driver's dwell alone.

The shortfall cannot be repaired by summing separate intervals. POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated traffic advisory of the right type, and EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no accumulation is available and no substituted account may stand in for it. Nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d): the arrival marker sits on a GPS fix at the same instant, the trace holds 25 fixes with no gap inside the waiting window, the chat holds exactly the 3 messages the trip record reports, and SGD 8.00 is the correct figure (the greater of the SGD 8.00 RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee and the SGD 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee), so it reconciles with the schedule. A COMPLETE, unimpaired artifact at weight 1.0 carries the deciding fact, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor.

Driver compensation is not payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (c) fails, so the 240-second hold earns nothing; the anti-farming check does not arise. The driver's conduct is recorded as a one-minute timing shortfall, not misconduct — he was present, stationary and willing at the correct bay.

No escalation trigger fires. There are no counterparty disputes between these parties in the trailing 90 days, the rider's trailing-30-day no-show dispute count is 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and the bundle is complete and unimpaired. Outcome: the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

What decides this case is the length of the driver's hold inside the pickup geofence, and both sides measure it the same way. POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four conditions hold together, and limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 seconds for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. The clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the driver tapping 'arrived'. On the trace the driver's single unbroken stationary interval runs 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 240 seconds against the 300-second minimum, a 60-second shortfall. Limbs (a) and (b) are made out (the trip record carries an 'arrived' event, and all 25 fixes place the driver about 24 m from the pin, well inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius), and limb (d) is made out (terminated by the driver with the recognised code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event). But the conditions are conjunctive; limb (c) fails, so the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-06 then governs and it is strict liability: where the effective in-geofence dwell falls below the minimum for the zone class, the cancellation fee is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The driver's own argument accepts this arithmetic, asking only that it be recorded as a timing defect rather than misconduct. It is recorded that way — the driver was present, stationary, and willing at the correct bay, and this is a one-minute timing shortfall, not an adverse finding. But the shortfall still defeats the charge.

The driver cannot repair it by summing intervals under POL-NS-06(i). The trace shows exactly one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to add to the first; and limb (i) additionally requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, whereas EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0). A MISSING artifact carries no fact, so limb (i) has nothing to operate on in any event. A missing advisory does not exonerate anyone and does not reduce the required minimum.

On the rider's side: POL-NS-04 is not available — the chat log holds only the system 'Your driver has arrived' notice and two driver messages, so no rider locating message exists (limb (a) fails), and the rider's own track sits about 519 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m rider-presence radius (limb (c) fails). That does not matter here: POL-NS-06 conditions the refund on the driver's dwell, not on the rider's presence or responsiveness. POL-NS-05 is not engaged either — at the arrival marker the driver was stationary 24 m from the pin, so neither the 300 m nor the 15 kph trigger is met and no false-arrival record arises.

POL-NS-07 pays the driver nothing, because it requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full and limb (c) is not satisfied. No anti-farming issue arises (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below 4, and 1/120 is far below 0.08), and that check is neutral in any case once compensation is already unavailable.

No evidence is impaired under POL-NS-08: the 'arrived' event sits on a GPS fix at the same instant (no clock skew), the trace holds 25 fixes with a zero-second maximum gap (no trace defect), the chat holds exactly the 3 messages the trip record reports (no chat defect), and the SGD 8.00 line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) (no fare defect). No POL-NS-09 trigger fires, and confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor, so the case is decided now rather than escalated. No clause produces a referral.

Because the deciding dwell measurement is carried by EV-GPS-09103 at weight 1.0, confidence is 0.9. The SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is returned to the rider; the driver receives no compensation; nothing outstanding requires a human reviewer.

The driver did arrive. The GPS trace places him about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura ride-hail bay pin — far inside the 120 m arrival radius that applies to a LARGE_VENUE pickup — stationary at 0 km/h across all 25 fixes, and the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event. Limbs (a) and (b) of POL-NS-01 are therefore met, and there is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05: at the 'arrived' timestamp the driver was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor moving at 15 km/h or above. The driver's account that he was present at the correct bay is corroborated, and the rider's 519 m distance from the pin confirms this is not a wrong-entrance case under POL-NS-03.

The fee nonetheless fails on the waiting period. POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence hold of at least the zone minimum — 300 seconds for LARGE_VENUE — measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix (17:15:00), not from the 'arrived' tap (17:15:20). The trace measures a single continuous hold of 240 seconds, a 60-second shortfall. Limb (c) fails, and under POL-NS-06 — which is strict liability and does not depend on where the rider was or whether she answered — the cancellation fee is refunded in full. Only one in-geofence interval exists, so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation cannot apply, and it could not apply in any event: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), and a missing artifact can carry no fact and cannot be asserted to excuse the shortfall.

The rider's own conduct does not change the refund. She was about 519 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes and sent no locating or coordinating message, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate her — but POL-NS-06 does not turn on that, and that route was never needed.

The driver receives no compensation. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not; a 240-second hold earns nothing. The anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d of 1 and a 1/120 rate of 0.008, both below their thresholds), so compensation is not withheld on that ground either — it is simply not payable.

No referral and no escalation.
